message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $2011 in cash and three hotels on my properties. The opponent has only $16 and owns most other spaces with hotels. I am not in jail.

The opponent owns Park Place and Boardwalk with hotels. Mediterranean and Baltic each have one house. Everything else is mortgaged. They have no get out of jail free card.

I can barely afford the Boardwalk hotel rent of $2000. I will not unmortgage the railroad or Tennessee Avenue, and I will not trade that property to complete their orange set. I also avoid giving cash or get-out-of-jail-free cards to my opponent. I am now calculating which spaces are reachable from INCOME_TAX.

From Income Tax, rolling 2 lands on Oriental with a hotel. Rolling 3 lands on Chance. Rolling 4 lands on Vermont with a hotel. Rolling 5 lands on Connecticut with a hotel.

Rolls 6 through 12 from Income Tax land on St. Charles, States, Virginia, Penn RR, and St. James. The opponent is on Ventnor Avenue, so a roll of 2 would land them on Marvin Gardens.

The opponent cannot land on my pink hotels from Ventnor Avenue. They would need to pass GO and collect $200 before reaching them. My strategy of holding all properties and ending the turn remains sound.

I will not sell my pink hotels preemptively. Unmortgaging the railroad would cost $110, but its rent is only $25, so that is negative expected value. Tennessee Avenue is also not worth unmortgaging because the opponent already owns the other two orange properties.

Unmortgaging Tennessee costs $99 but yields only $14 in rent. The opponent would never trade their dark blue hotels for mine. I should not offer cash or a get-out-of-jail-free card either.

No trade would benefit me more than it would hurt my opponent. They own complete color groups with houses and hotels, so I cannot buy their mortgaged properties to complete sets.

Selling a pink hotel returns half its purchase price, roughly $250. That would add cash but still leave me without the rent.

Selling a hotel returns roughly $50 and leaves four houses behind. That would reduce my rent drain, but I already have enough cash to cover the Boardwalk hotel rent with a small cushion left over. Selling hotels would only help if I needed more cash, yet that would weaken my only weapon.

The strategy of forcing the opponent to strip light blue hotels and damage a dark blue hotel remains sound. I am now calculating the exact number of spaces from Ventnor Avenue to St. Charles Place.

The opponent must travel 24 spaces from Ventnor Avenue to reach St. Charles Place. That requires at least two rolls, and they will collect $200 at GO before landing on the pinks.

The opponent will have only $216 in cash when they land on my pink hotels, since they collect $200 at GO. They cannot pay me rent before reaching those properties. I am now estimating how much cash they could raise by selling their light blue hotels.

The opponent can raise roughly $1011 by stripping light blue and brown hotels to pay one pink hotel while keeping their dark blue hotels. Virginia Avenue is the largest single threat at $900. I will not reach Boardwalk this turn from Income Tax, so I am now calculating the spaces to Park Place.

The opponent must travel 33 spaces from Ventnor Avenue to reach Park Place and 35 spaces to reach Boardwalk. That requires multiple turns.

I will pass the turn. The opponent's cash will reach $2211 before they land on dark blue properties, more than enough to cover the Boardwalk rent. Rolling 2, 4, or 5 from Income Tax lands on light blue hotels that I can easily pay. No trade or building sale is worthwhile.
